references.text: Ezekiel describes God's promise to gather the scattered sheep from all nations and bring them back under one shepherd, which directly foreshadows Jesus' statement about 'other sheep' that will become one flock under one shepherd.

Here it is proclaimed that David shall be one shepherd over all, and that the people shall become one nation, a clear parallel theme to Jesus' prophecy of one flock and one shepherd uniting different groups.
Yahweh promises to gather those who are scattered and adds that He will gather even more to join those already gathered, reflecting the idea of 'other sheep' not belonging to the current fold.
John explains that Jesus died to gather God's scattered children into one, which is the theological explanation of how the 'other sheep' become one flock.
Paul describes how Christ has made the two (Jews and Gentiles) one by breaking down the dividing wall, realizing Jesus' vision of one flock from previously separated groups.
